paper_title: RLHF Workflow From Reward Modeling to Online RLHF
caption: Evaluation of our models and LLaMA-3-8B-inst.
model_annotation: The bar chart titled "Model Evaluation on Academic and Practical Benchmarks" compares the performance of two models—LLaMA-3-8B-it (blue bars) and Ours (Iterative RLHF) (orange bars)—across eight different datasets and metrics. The horizontal axis, labeled "Dataset and Metrics," lists the benchmarks in the following order: GSM-8K, MMLU, HumanEval, TruthfulQA, ARC, MBPP, LC AlpacaEval2, MT-Bench (×.5), and Chat-Arena-Hard. The vertical axis, labeled "Score (%)", ranges from 0 to 80 with tick marks at intervals of 10, representing the percentage score achieved by each model on each benchmark. For most benchmarks, the orange bars (Ours) are slightly taller than the blue bars (LLaMA-3-8B-it), indicating a modest performance improvement. For example, on GSM-8K, LLaMA-3-8B-it scores approximately 80%, while Ours scores around 82%. On MMLU, the scores are approximately 68% and 70%, respectively. On HumanEval, scores are around 62% and 65%. On TruthfulQA, LLaMA-3-8B-it scores about 45% and Ours scores around 60%. On ARC, scores are approximately 60% and 65%. On MBPP, scores are about 60% and 62%. On LC AlpacaEval2, LLaMA-3-8B-it scores around 20% and Ours scores about 30%. On MT-Bench (×.5), scores are approximately 40% and 45%. On Chat-Arena-Hard, LLaMA-3-8B-it scores around 20% and Ours scores about 30%. The bars are grouped by benchmark, with the two models presented side-by-side for direct comparison. The chart uses a legend in the top-right corner to identify the models by color. There is no explicit sorting of benchmarks by performance, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding.
